title: Avalanche: Optimizing Cache Utilization via Matrix Reordering for Sparse Matrix Multiplication Accelerator
problem: Sparse Matrix Multiplication (SpMM) accelerators suffer from poor on-chip memory utilization due to irregular memory access patterns; existing designs fail to cache both input matrices efficiently, leading to redundant DRAM accesses and low throughput.
method: Avalanche applies three complementary techniques: (1) Mat-Reorder reorders columns of matrix B to maximize data locality and enable early completion of row computations in matrix A; (2) DP-Evict (Dead-Product Early Eviction) immediately evicts fully-computed intermediate products from on-chip SRAM to reclaim capacity; (3) RM-Caching (Reuse Distance-Aware Matrix Caching) prioritizes retention of matrix B elements with short reuse distances in the on-chip cache. Together these techniques keep both operand matrices resident in a 6.15 mm2 chip with minimal spill-to-DRAM.

title: Efficient Recycling Subspace Truncation Method for Periodic Small-Signal Analysis
problem: Krylov subspace recycling for periodic small-signal RF analysis accelerates simulation but increasing memory cost becomes a bottleneck in large-scale designs; restarting loses recycling benefits.
method: Proposes recycling subspace truncation framework with efficient initial guess selection method and Floquet-based subspace truncation strategy to reduce memory while maintaining iteration benefits.

title: Hopps: Leveraging Sparsity to Accelerate Automata Processing
problem: Automata processing (AP) workloads execute many finite state machines (FSMs) in parallel over streaming symbol data, but existing AP accelerators suffer poor utilization because most FSMs are inactive (in a non-matching state) for any given input symbol. The irregular, state-dependent activation pattern makes it hard to exploit spatial parallelism efficiently.
method: Hopps exploits the observation that only a sparse subset of FSMs transition on each input symbol. It uses a sparsity-aware representation that tracks only active states across all FSMs and a compressed activation bitmap to skip idle FSMs entirely during each symbol step. The architecture couples this with a tiled SRAM storage layout so that state-transition tables for active FSMs are fetched in bursts, reducing off-chip memory traffic proportional to the active-FSM fraction.

title: SeIM: In-Memory Acceleration for Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search
problem: ANNS workloads bottleneck on memory bandwidth (extensive random access) and sorting (cross-memory-unit data dependencies), limiting throughput in CPU/GPU/ASIC-based systems and making them inefficient for RAG-based LLM inference.
method: Hierarchical in-memory architecture that offloads memory-bound parallel ANNS operations (vector loading, distance computation) to the memory bank level with minimal DRAM modifications, and places compute-bound sorting at the memory controller level with adaptive transmission filtering to reduce cross-unit data transfers during merge operations.

title: 15.2 A 1024-Channel 0.00029mm2/ch 74nW/ch Online Spatial Spike-Sorting Chip with Event-Driven Spike Detection and Self-Organizing Map Clustering
problem: High-density multi-electrode arrays (HD-MEA) for brain-computer interfaces generate massive raw spike data that must be reduced on-chip for wireless operation. Prior spike-sorting (SS) designs either require large input buffers, use temporal features that don't scale to multi-channel systems, access entire clustering memory per spike, or consume high power and area.
method: A 1024-channel spike-sorting chip uses event-driven spike detection (only processes spike events, not raw samples) and spatial spike-sorting (uses waveform shape, not time features) with self-organizing map (SOM) clustering. Event-driven and spatial approaches avoid large buffers, scale to multi-channel systems, and eliminate per-spike full-memory accesses.

title: Generalizing Reuse Patterns for Efficient DNN on Microcontrollers
problem: DNN inference on microcontrollers is limited by their restricted compute and memory, and existing computation reuse techniques that exploit redundancy in input/activation data are constrained by a narrow definition of reuse patterns, leaving a large portion of potential reuse unexploited.
method: The work introduces generalized reuse, which frames computation reuse in terms of row and column reordering of a matrix view of DNN input or activation maps. By recognizing that different reorderings expose different reuse patterns, the approach dramatically expands the explorable reuse space beyond what prior narrow pattern definitions allow. Two analytical models are developed: one predicts the accuracy impact of a given reuse pattern (approximate computation), and one predicts latency on the target microcontroller. These models enable efficient search over the generalized reuse space to select patterns that best trade off accuracy and speed for a given DNN and hardware.

title: Introducing Instruction-Accurate Simulators for Performance Estimation of Autotuning Workloads
problem: Autotuning ML workloads typically requires execution on target hardware to evaluate implementation variants, but target hardware availability is limited. Scalability is constrained by hardware access when exploring large optimization spaces.
method: Framework enables autotuning workload execution on instruction-accurate simulators (not target hardware). Machine learning predictors trained on simulation statistics forecast performance on target hardware. Evaluated on x86, ARM, and RISC-V simulators; predictors consistently identify the best implementation in top 3% of predictions.

title: "Zen 5": The AMD High-Performance 4nm x86-64 Microprocessor Core
problem: Client, server, and embedded x86 markets demand high per-core performance and energy efficiency within a fixed area budget. AMD must balance clock frequency (5.7GHz target), instruction throughput, and power consumption across diverse workloads.
method: Zen 5 is a 55mm² core complex (CCX) with 8 cores in TSMC 4nm FinFET, each with 1MB L2 and shared 32MB L3 cache. The design uses configurable FP256/FP512 datapaths to support diverse vector workloads. Microarchitecture enhancements include improved branch prediction, better I-cache prefetching, additional rename registers, and TLB optimization. A Zen 5c variant optimizes for density and power efficiency in key markets.

title: 30.6 A 64Gb DDR4 STT-MRAM Using a Time-Controlled Discharge-Reading Scheme for a .001681µm 1T-1MTJ Cross-Point Cell
problem: High-density 1-selector-1-magnetoresistive-tunneling-junction (1S1M) MRAM arrays require reliable read operations that maximize read signal while minimizing read disturbance; conventional read schemes struggle with dense cross-point topologies.
method: A timing-controlled discharge-read scheme combined with local-capacitance mode enables reliable read/write in high-density 1S1M arrays; the approach optimizes discharge timing to balance read signal amplitude and disturbance margins.

title: 2.3 Granite Rapids-D: Intel Xeon 6 SoC for vRAN, Edge, Networking, and Storage
problem: vRAN (virtualized radio access networks), edge servers, networking, and storage workloads have diverging requirements: compute-optimized SKUs need scalar/data-parallel performance with low-latency high-bandwidth memory; edge SKUs require rugged operation (-40°C to 85°C) with dynamic temperature support.
method: Granite Rapids-D (GNR-D): Intel Xeon 6 SoC offering dual optimization strategies: (1) compute-optimized SKU with high scalar/parallel throughput, PCIe5, low-latency memory for data-center edge and vRAN; (2) edge-optimized SKU rated for rugged -40°C to 85°C operation with full dynamic range thermal support. Integrated confidential AI security (TEE) and ethernet/accelerator support across both classes.

title: Micro-MAMA: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Multicore Prefetching
problem: Independent RL-based prefetchers on each core of a multicore system compete for shared memory bandwidth without coordination, causing each agent to greedily claim excessive bandwidth and converging to sub-optimal system-wide policies. This problem is an instance of the multi-agent credit assignment and non-stationarity challenge in MARL.
method: MAMA uses a two-tier architecture: distributed local multi-armed bandit agents on each core narrow the joint-action search space by selecting among local prefetch aggressiveness options, while a central supervisor agent with global bandwidth visibility learns joint policies that maximize system-wide throughput or fairness. Key local agents receive system-level perspective signals (estimated global bandwidth usage) to discourage actions that harm other cores. The supervisor uses a lightweight bandit over the local agents' reduced action space, avoiding the exponential joint-action blow-up of fully centralized control.

title: A 0.9pJ/b 108Gb/s PAM-4 VCSEL-Based Direct-Drive Optical Engine
problem: Electrical interconnects for high-throughput data centers face scalability limits due to power-hungry equalization and DSP; pluggable optical modules add re-timer complexity and latency; co-packaged optics (CPO) requires efficient direct-drive without DSP re-timing.
method: A PAM-4 VCSEL-based direct-drive optical engine integrates VCSEL driver and transimpedance amplifier using: (1) coupled-inductor CZ-CTIE for VCSEL complex-pole equalization, (2) high-linearity differential TIA for large optical modulation, (3) active CZ-CTIE for TIA shunt-feedback compensation.

title: 6.4 A 400×400 3.24μm 117dB-Dynamic-Range 3-Layer Stacked Digital Pixel Sensor
problem: AR/VR glasses and compact cameras require small pixel sizes with HDR capture and low power consumption; existing 2-layer stacked DPS at larger pixels cannot meet form-factor demands while supporting AI/CV processing.
method: 3-layer stacked digital pixel sensor with single-ended comparator-based ADC, optimized control logic, and 10b in-pixel SRAM in each pixel. Single-exposure HDR via per-pixel exposure time control. Frame averaging unit (FAU) and ISP on-die for FPN correction. Sparse transmission enables AI/CV acceleration.

title: 25.4 A Micromachined Heterogeneously Integrated Active-Probe Enabling Non-Disruptive In-Situ Measurements from DC to 50GHz
problem: Debugging and failure analysis of densely integrated microsystems require probing at tight pitches with minimal signal distortion, but traditional 50Ω test equipment introduces excessive capacitive and inductive loading at microscale interfaces.
method: Micromachined probe substrate heterogeneously integrated with high-performance RF sense amplifier; high-Z probe design minimizes capacitive/inductive loading at test point, while integrated sense amp enables low-noise signal acquisition from DC to 50GHz.

title: Qtenon: Towards Low-Latency Architecture Integration for Accelerating Hybrid Quantum-Classical Computing
problem: Hybrid quantum-classical algorithms are bottlenecked by the decoupled architecture of current quantum hardware systems, which lacks low-latency communication channels and fine-grained software control for tightly coordinating quantum and classical computation. The high round-trip latency between host processor and quantum accelerator prevents real-time feedback loops required by variational algorithms.
method: Qtenon is a RISC-V extended chip implemented in Chisel that tightly couples classical and quantum processing via three hardware components: a unified memory hierarchy serving as a shared communication buffer between the host and quantum accelerators, an efficient quantum controller with dedicated data paths, and a multi-stage processing pipeline that exploits instruction-level parallelism across quantum-classical interaction phases. A custom ISA extension provides instructions for data communication, computation, fine-grained synchronization, and efficient scheduling of quantum-host interaction.

title: A 4.69mW LLM Processor with Binary/Ternary Weights for Billion-Parameter Llama Model
problem: Running billion-parameter LLMs on edge devices requires extreme power efficiency; standard precision weights consume orders of magnitude more power than practical for mobile/IoT.
method: The processor uses binary and ternary weight quantization (extreme 1-2 bit precision) combined with specialized compute units optimized for low-precision arithmetic. Custom dataflow exploits weight sparsity patterns from quantization, reducing memory bandwidth and computation.
